svg.title: One bypass can change overload outcomes under a fixed schedule
svg.desc: Begin after A: O = 6, R = 3, H = 2, U = 1; waiting queue limit = 2 records
svg.text: One bypass can change overload outcomes under a fixed schedule
Begin after A: O = 6, R = 3, H = 2, U = 1; waiting queue limit = 2 records
B needs 2 credits; S and T each need 1
B arrives first and waits. FIFO holds S behind B.
One-bypass policy admits S, then freezes further bypass of B.
T arrives: outcome depends on queue occupancy
FIFO: queue [B,S] is full, so T is rejected.
Bypass: queue [B,T] fits; T must wait behind B.
Safe returns create the two credits B needs
After the prescribed S/J returns, both policies admit B.
B completes without growth; its block and unused credit safely release.
FIFO completes B and S; bypass completes S, B and T.
Both end O = 5, R = 3, H = 2, U = 2, with an empty waiting queue.
Event order is not elapsed time. A bounded bypass count does not guarantee a waiting-time bound.
